q: AGENTS.md's test placement rule in goose is:
options: Prefer the tests/ folder (e.g. crates/goose/tests/) for integration tests over in-src test modules
Keep all tests inside src/ modules to reduce compile time
Write every test at the workspace root in a single tests.rs
Prefer doctests over compiled tests
explanation: The rule is the opposite — prefer tests/ over src-internal modules where possible.
Root-level single-file tests don't exist in this workspace layout.
Doctests have a role but the rule says prefer tests/ folder.

q: The MockProvider in mcp_integration_test.rs is built by:
options: Implementing the real Provider trait (plus descriptor traits) inline in the test file
Subclassing a special TestProvider base class
Generating code from the provider's OpenAPI spec
Recording a real provider binary to disk
explanation: Rust has no class inheritance; the mock implements the trait directly.
Provider specs are not used to generate mocks in this repo.
Recording real providers is not how the mock is defined.

options: Builds goose-test, runs the MCP integration test with GOOSE_RECORD_MCP=1, then stages crates/goose/tests/mcp_replays/
Deletes old replays, runs cargo test once, then force-pushes the replay branch
Runs the MCP server under valgrind and saves its heap profile
Fetches upstream replays from a remote object store and cherry-picks them
explanation: Recording re-runs the live seam and stages the new artifacts; it does not delete or push.
No profiler is involved in the record path.
Replays are generated locally from the real server, not downloaded.

q: In mcp_integration_test.rs:199, replay mode (GOOSE_RECORD_MCP unset) means:
options: The test serves responses from previously recorded artifacts instead of hitting a live server
The test skips all assertions
The test runs against a randomly chosen public MCP server
The test re-records automatically every run
explanation: Replays still assert outcomes; only the server seam is swapped for stored data.
Nondeterministic external servers are exactly what replays avoid.
Automatic re-recording would silently mutate committed evidence — recording is explicit.

q: Why are recorded MCP replays committed to git?
options: They are reviewed evidence of real wire behavior, and tests must not silently drift from them
They compress better than source code
CI cannot run tests without a network connection otherwise
GitHub requires all test data be stored in LFS
explanation: Storage size is not the criterion for committing fixture data.
Network independence is a benefit, not the review reason — drift control is.
No GitHub rule mandates replay fixtures be committed.

q: Which is a valid in-process MCP test fixture shipped by goose-test-support?
options: McpFixtureServer exposing get_code/get_image/get_audience_content tools over rmcp
A docker-compose stack of five real MCP servers
A mock that always returns HTTP 500
A Wireshark packet-capture harness
explanation: goose-test-support is a Rust fixture crate, no containers involved.
A fixture simulating only failures would be useless for happy-path tests.
Packet capture is not part of the Rust test fixture surface.

q: Fix this compile error in a test: `error[E0277]: the trait bound 'MockProvider: Provider' is not satisfied`. The cleanest fix per goose doctrine:
options: Implement the missing Provider trait methods (stream, get_name, ...) on MockProvider rather than changing the tested code
Delete the trait bound from the function signature
Add `#![allow(incomplete_features)]` to the test file
Rewrite the test to call the provider's private fields directly
explanation: Removing the bound weakens the API the test claims to exercise — the seam disappears.
Feature gates do not implement traits.
Reaching into private fields breaks the public-API discipline the tests/ layer exists for.
